name: Short stature due to partial Growth Hormone Receptor (GHR) deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for partial GHR deficiency

criteria.description: Short stature with height below the 3rd percentile for age and sex
Reduced serum IGF-1 levels despite normal or elevated growth hormone levels
Identification of pathogenic variants in the GHR gene consistent with partial receptor deficiency
Poor or suboptimal growth response to exogenous growth hormone therapy
Exclusion of other causes of short stature including nutritional, endocrine, and systemic diseases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of short stature with low IGF-1 levels despite normal/elevated GH and confirmed pathogenic GHR gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires molecular genetic confirmation and biochemical evaluation.

laboratory: Low serum IGF-1 levels despite normal or elevated serum growth hormone
Normal or mildly elevated insulin levels
imaging: Delayed bone age on hand/wrist X-ray
other: Poor or suboptimal growth response to recombinant human growth hormone therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Complete GHR deficiency with more severe short stature
Markedly elevated serum growth hormone levels
Absent or very low IGF-1 levels
Low or absent serum growth hormone levels
Improved growth response to GH therapy
Characteristic phenotypic features such as webbed neck and lymphedema

redFlags: Severe growth failure below the 1st percentile
Lack of response to growth hormone therapy
Presence of additional systemic abnormalities or dysmorphic features
